splat.section: MATTER — what things are made of
splat.definition: an anisotropic 3D Gaussian: a position, a covariance (its size and shape and orientation in one 3×3 matrix), a colour and an opacity. The primitive the whole pipeline is built on, because it is simultaneously a rendering primitive and a *statistical* one. A splat is not a triangle and not a voxel: it has no surface and no fixed extent.

gaussian splatting / 3dgs.section: MATTER — what things are made of
gaussian splatting / 3dgs.definition: representing a scene as millions of splats fitted to photographs. What a "scan" is in this repo.

genome.section: MATTER — what things are made of
genome.definition: the compressed description of one kind of matter. Two halves: **morphology-DNA** (shape) and **material-DNA** (appearance). Stored as **distributions**, never single values.

material-dna.section: MATTER — what things are made of
material-dna.definition: the *splat configuration*: the joint distribution of size, anisotropy, angle, colour and opacity across a material's splats. Deliberately a **range, not an average** — the range is what lets you generate new members of the same kind.

morphology-dna.section: MATTER — what things are made of
morphology-dna.definition: the shape half: how the pieces are placed. See **arrangement**.

feature.section: MATTER — what things are made of
feature.definition: one measured axis of a genome (`size`, `aniso`, `R`, `G`, `B`, `opacity`), each stored as `mean` + `p10..p90`.

anisotropy.section: MATTER — what things are made of
anisotropy.definition: `1 - min_axis/max_axis` of a splat's covariance. 0 = a sphere, 1 = a needle. Bounded [0,1] **by construction**, which is why it must be sampled on the **liability scale**.

serial number.section: MATTER — what things are made of
serial number.definition: the codebook index of a *recognised* genome. Compression made literal: once a material is in the codebook you store the serial instead of the splats. Position- derived for places (`S+00384+00896`), genome-derived for matter.

brick.section: MATTER — what things are made of
brick.definition: a genome expressed as a placeable object: a **membrane** carrying that genome's measured properties plus a mating **stud**. The LEGO metaphor made precise.

intake method.section: MATTER — what things are made of
intake method.definition: how a genome was obtained. Exactly two: **MEASURED** (scan → inverse rendering → *reality*) and **AUTHORED** (GLB/OBJ PBR maps read directly → *an artist*). Both feed one codebook, which is why **format calibration** matters.

format calibration.section: MATTER — what things are made of
format calibration.definition: making different file formats agree numerically before they enter the codebook. An uncalibrated container **forks the same material into two serial numbers**. Proven case: INRIA `.ply` stores colour as an SH DC coefficient (`rgb = 0.5 + 0.28209479177387814·f_dc`); applying `sigmoid()` instead gave p10 0.143 vs a true 0.000. → `Construction/calibrate_formats.py` ---

arrangement.section: ARRANGEMENT — how the pieces are placed
arrangement.definition: the structural archetype of an object: *where the pieces go*, as opposed to what a piece looks like. The operator's point: what must be learned is **how the pieces fit**. Measured by four facts, all scale-free.

clustering.section: ARRANGEMENT — how the pieces are placed
clustering.definition: mean pairwise distance ÷ nearest-neighbour distance. High = pieces gather into distinct groups; low = evenly scattered. **The number that exposed the vocabulary gap**: real truck-scan regions measure 4.679–8.172, while the three hand-written forms reached only 1.277–1.497. Real matter is 3–5× more clustered than the old vocabulary could express.

verticality.section: ARRANGEMENT — how the pieces are placed
verticality.definition: the mean |z| component of piece directions. 0 = everything lying flat, 1 = everything standing up.

alignment.section: ARRANGEMENT — how the pieces are placed
alignment.definition: how parallel the pieces are to each other (mean resultant length of their directions). 1 = perfectly combed, 0 = random. Real material sits at **partial** coherence (0.516–0.576) — neither combed nor random.

aspect.section: ARRANGEMENT — how the pieces are placed
aspect.definition: horizontal extent ÷ vertical extent of the whole arrangement.

band.section: ARRANGEMENT — how the pieces are placed
band.definition: the measured min..max of a fact across real regions. The training target is a band, **not a value**, because real material varies from region to region and demanding a single number would be fitting noise.

band error.section: ARRANGEMENT — how the pieces are placed
band error.definition: distance OUTSIDE a band, normalised by that band's own width; zero anywhere inside. Normalisation is load-bearing: clustering spans 3.49 and alignment spans 0.06, so a raw sum would weight clustering 58× for no physical reason.

band margin.section: ARRANGEMENT — how the pieces are placed
band margin.definition: how far a genome sits from the nearest band edge. 1.0 = dead centre of every band, 0.0 = on an edge. **Why it exists:** the first trained winner satisfied every constraint with `verticality 0.476` against a `0.476` ceiling — inside by zero, with nowhere to vary. Adding margin as a maximize raised child survival from **38% → 81%**. Margin is physics, not taste: *a genome with room on all sides has children that are still real material.*

form.section: ARRANGEMENT — how the pieces are placed
form.definition: the named arrangement an emitter uses. `tuft`/`clump`/`shard` are hand-written guesses; **`measured`** is the trained one and is now the default. ---

genotype.section: GENETICS — used literally, not as metaphor
genotype.definition: the stored distribution. **phenotype** — the expressed splat cloud. The distinction is load-bearing: the DSL *is* the genotype, physics is the decompressor.

heritability.section: GENETICS — used literally, not as metaphor
heritability.definition: `V_between / (V_between + V_within)`: the fraction of variation that **breeds true**. **Undefined from a single specimen**, which is why two scans of a kind are the minimum useful sample. → `core/progeny.py :: heritability()`

linkage group.section: GENETICS — used literally, not as metaphor
linkage group.definition: traits inherited as a block. `colour` = (R,G,B), `form` = (size, aniso), `body` = (opacity).

pleiotropy.section: GENETICS — used literally, not as metaphor
pleiotropy.definition: one underlying factor driving several traits. R/G/B are driven largely by luminance. **Why it matters:** sampling R, G and B independently produced *rainbow confetti* children; sharing a luminance factor fixed it.

recombination.section: GENETICS — used literally, not as metaphor
recombination.definition: a child draws each linkage group from one of two parents (**independent assortment**), so siblings differ in whole blocks rather than in noise.

mutation.section: GENETICS — used literally, not as metaphor
mutation.definition: a separate, low-rate perturbation. **Not** the same thing as parental variance; conflating the two is why one-parent sampling looked like noise.

liability scale.section: GENETICS — used literally, not as metaphor
liability scale.definition: modelling a bounded trait on an unbounded scale and transforming back (**logit** for proportions, **log** for positives). **Why:** a Gaussian drawn directly on a [0,1] trait with mean 0.95 piles probability on the boundary — children came out saturated white and sizes drew negative. The inverse transform cannot leave the domain, so no clamping is ever needed. Fixed 0/10 saturated after.

plasticity.section: GENETICS — used literally, not as metaphor
plasticity.definition: one genotype expressed differently by environment. That is the **verb** and the **membrane**. Not inherited.

progeny / children.section: GENETICS — used literally, not as metaphor
progeny / children.definition: variations of one isolated object, sampled from its measured ranges. The operator's correction: you do not paint a material onto a surface (that is texturing) — you isolate ONE object, generate variations, and **place instances**. ---

membrane.definition: a boundary, and therefore **a scale**. The project's core primitive. It supplies six things at once: a local frame, a local unit, an identity, an inside/outside test, a level of detail, and a set of **ports**. Nested membranes *are* the hierarchy.

why it is the primitive.definition: a boundary is what makes a cause **attributable**. In biology the vesicle is what lets a replicator keep what it makes (no inside/outside → no individual attribute an outcome to a change rather than to the world.
code: nothing for selection to act on). In engineering the same boundary is what lets you

skin.definition: the thickness of "on the boundary", in metres (default 1 mm). **Why absolute:** a relative tolerance of `1e-6 × scale` on a planet-radius membrane made "on the surface" mean ±6.4 m, so `side()` returned `'on'` for everything.

port / stud.definition: a typed interface on a membrane, typed by **what flows** through it: `structural`, `gravitational`, `energy`, `fluid`, `atmospheric`, `substrate`. Not a category — a physical claim.

mate.definition: attach a brick to a port. After mating the port is no longer open, and the child records `attached_via`. **Why recorded rather than inferred:** `open_ports()` used to infer occupancy from geometry and reported "filled 0" with six bricks attached.

the six directions.definition: the ports of a cell (±X, ±Y, ±Z). Used as a **development-focus mechanism**: pick one direction and build it out. Distance travelled is not a consideration; the mechanism must transcend scales.

work queue.definition: the list of unfilled studs. *Where the world is unfinished*, enumerated.

saturated.definition: a membrane with no open ports. Its state becomes `MIGRATE`.

time as the outermost membrane.definition: the fourth dimension is a membrane like any other: the past inside, the future outside, the present its surface. A game with a beginning and an end is a set of states between 0 and 1.

cell.definition: the human-scale unit, **1.83 m (6 ft)**. Earth's surface is 1.52e14 cells.

section.definition: a 128 m tile, addressed by position (`S+00384+00896`). Sections never have to agree with their neighbours about anything, because content is **deterministic by coordinate**. → `core/sections.py`

deterministic by coordinate.definition: content derives from a pure function of position (`tile_seed(ix,iy)`, `world_height(x,y)`), so the same seed gives the same world forever and seams match without negotiation. Measured seam continuity: **5.8e-10**. ---

verb.definition: a range between two states of a noun. To make a verb you need a noun that has two states and a **dial** between them. THRUST, BALANCE, GROW, CONNECT, SCAN, NAVIGATE_ORBIT.

two ends and a dial.definition: the single mechanism underneath verbs, morphs, heritability, LOD, growth and the story. `Anchor` / `Axis` / `Dial`. → `Construction/scene.py`

gate.definition: a dial held until a **measured** condition holds. How game progression is expressed without scripting it. *(Distinct from the verification gates in §7 — same word, different layer.)* ---

train, don't hand-tune.definition: if a feature is **DATA** (prices, damage, yields, morphology, layouts), do not tune it by reasoning. An LLM manages ~20 edits/hour; `core/trainer.py` does ~30,000 evals/sec. Six orders of magnitude.

domain.definition: `core/trainables/<f>.py`, providing `seed` / `mutate` / `measure`. Reports **FACTS only, never opinions**. → e.g. `core/trainables/arrangement.py`

objective.definition: `docs/objectives/<f>.json`, saying which facts are GOOD. Written by the LLM. Must contain at least one **maximize** term or you get a **satisficer**.

the llm sits at the top and the bottom,.term: the LLM sits at the top and the bottom, never the middle
the llm sits at the top and the bottom,.definition: it writes the constraints and reads the walls; it never turns the crank.

measure.definition: the domain's report. A fact, not a judgement. `measure(genome) -> dict`.

pinned.definition: the walls the winner is **riding**. The trainer names them. A pinned constraint is where the next exploit lives.

the exploit is the product.definition: a degenerate winner is not a failure. It is the optimiser auditing your spec at 35 kHz and finding the hole you would have defended in review.

iterate the objective, never the artifac.term: iterate the objective, never the artifact
iterate the objective, never the artifac.definition: when the winner is wrong, the *spec* is wrong. Worked example in this repo: round 1 of `arrangement` scored 0.9680 and landed inside all four bands — and was unusable, because nothing had asked for **band margin**.

satisficer.definition: an optimiser with no maximize term. It stops as soon as the constraints are met, which is almost never where you want it.

robustness.definition: `worst / mean` across N randomised restarts. A real limit cycle is ~1.0; a fraud is ~0. **One rollout from one initial condition is not a measurement — it is a coin toss.** Proven: a celebrated 13.52-body-length walker had `periodicity 0.25` and lost 5.5 body lengths to a **one-micron** nudge; under honest physics it scored *worse than an untrained brain* after 80,000 evaluations of selecting lucky dice.

reachability probe.definition: checking what the domain can actually reach *before* setting a hard gate. **A gate you cannot reach is not strict, it is blind:** score-zero everywhere means no gradient, and the trainer degenerates into a random walk while appearing to run at full speed. Measured case: 0/140 random arrangement genomes reached `clustering >= 4.5`.

hard gate.definition: a constraint whose violation scores **zero**. Use only where the initial population can already satisfy it, or where nothing is near it yet (a guard against overshoot, e.g. `clustering <= 12`).

self-loading reference.definition: a domain that loads its own measured target and **raises** if it is missing. `material_appearance` trained against `None` for weeks because nothing checked. ---

research gate.section: VERIFICATION — the gates, in the order they fire
research gate.definition: refuses a research-less session unless sources are cited or a reasoned waiver is recorded. → `core/research_gate.py`

witness gate.section: VERIFICATION — the gates, in the order they fire
witness gate.definition: a feature cannot be recorded `verified`/`observed` without an observation node. **A compile is not proof.** → `core/witness_gate.py`

visual gate.section: VERIFICATION — the gates, in the order they fire
visual gate.definition: additionally requires a recorded LM screenshot analysis. The model must have **looked** at it. → `core/visual_gate.py`

training gate.section: VERIFICATION — the gates, in the order they fire
training gate.definition: `verified` requires curriculum enrolment and reps begun. The unit of training is **the piece you worked**. → `core/training_gate.py`

the coin.section: VERIFICATION — the gates, in the order they fire
the coin.definition: every verification has two faces: **HEADS = the claim**, **TAILS = the evidence**. Both are judged, in both directions. Not the same coin → refused.

the why loop.section: VERIFICATION — the gates, in the order they fire
the why loop.definition: **a why IS an edge**, not a computed report. `A --because--> B` answers "why A?", so asking why **writes** the graph. Exactly two legal terminals: **PHYSICS** (true in an empty universe) and **THE HUMAN** (taste, and it is earned). **An LLM is never a terminal** — its answer is another claim, so the walk recurses past it.

a field can lie; an edge cannot.term: A field can lie; an edge cannot
a field can lie; an edge cannot.section: VERIFICATION — the gates, in the order they fire
a field can lie; an edge cannot.definition: a graph knows its own ids. Measured before it existed: 1,448 edges and *not one* meant BECAUSE; 150 finalized claims carried zero recorded whys.

membrane (verification sense).section: VERIFICATION — the gates, in the order they fire
membrane (verification sense).definition: `python -m core.membrane run --burn -- <cmd>` runs a command in a sealed copy of the studio and then **proves** it touched nothing live. It *measures* its containment instead of asserting it. Seals a git worktree of the current tree **plus `docs/world/`** — which is gitignored, so a worktree alone would leave the DNA graph shared with live. That is the difference between a membrane and a costume. ---

rung.definition: one level of the bottom-up chain, each trained separately against reality's own numbers, each handing the next its **averages** as data: ``` sand (40.03° emergent repose) → cloud → star (96% collapse) → embryos → solar systems (Kepler slope 1.50 at r²=1.000) → planets → climates → matter under boots ```

rung conflation.definition: a **named failure mode**: assembling a lower rung's parts while settling a higher rung's dynamics. Five trained rounds and a granularity probe all failed until the rungs were split; then the *untrained* smoke test succeeded. The fix was "think of the planet as ONE when we get to that scale."

lod of meaning.definition: each level of detail is the rung below's **average**. Approach = decompression; retreat = coalesce. **No aesthetic passes:** appearance DERIVES from the matter model at every scale, or the model is incomplete.

emergence.definition: a macro-number nobody coded, arising from local rules. **You do not call for it — you SELECT for it**: local rule = genome, emergent macro-numbers = measure, researched reality = objective. Proven: sand's 40.03° repose angle, Kepler's third law (slope 1.483–1.50, r² 0.9998–1.000) measured from grown orbits' own winding periods.

negative space.definition: the environment as **frozen cells** that an object must grow around. "The regolith is negative space that the object must grow around." ---

the gpu is mandatory.definition: for rendering, segmentation, DNA recovery and training. Measured: **2,358 evals/sec at 16,384 worlds** vs pybullet's 70 with 8 P-cores at thermal limit.

the one rule.definition: *nothing reads back from the GPU inside the rollout loop.* A previous attempt did 1,575 CPU↔GPU syncs per batch and ran **300× slower than the CPU**.

membrane vs faraday cage.definition: the membrane does not isolate the network. It is a cell wall. ---

ruliology.section: RULIOLOGY — borrowed vocabulary, and what it corrected here
ruliology.definition: systematically enumerating **all possible** simple programs of a type and observing what they do, instead of studying the ones somebody happened to write. The method this project already uses on genomes; now it has a name.

the axelrod error.section: RULIOLOGY — borrowed vocabulary, and what it corrected here
the axelrod error.definition: drawing conclusions from the programs people happened to submit. Wolfram's example: the famous 1980 prisoner's-dilemma tournament crowned **tit-for-tat**, but enumerating all 22 distinct 2-state machines ranks it **far down** — the real winner is "grim trigger", which nobody submitted. **Our instance of the same error:** `tuft`, `clump` and `shard` were three arrangements a person authored, and measurement showed them landing inside **zero** of reality's four bands. Hand-authored vocabularies are not samples of the possible; they are samples of what somebody thought of.

computational irreducibility.section: RULIOLOGY — borrowed vocabulary, and what it corrected here
computational irreducibility.definition: there is no shortcut: to know how something turns out you have to run it. Wolfram's conclusion about competition, and this studio's reason for the trainer — an LLM cannot reason its way to an answer at ~20 edits/hour that 30,000 evals/sec finds by running.

pocket of computational reducibility.section: RULIOLOGY — borrowed vocabulary, and what it corrected here
pocket of computational reducibility.definition: a region where behaviour *is* predictable, which is where systematic winners come from. **The sharper statement of what "trainable" means:** this project's DATA-vs-CODE split is a crude proxy for "does this feature have a pocket of reducibility?" A feature is trainable when a measurable objective has a searchable gradient into one.

capacity.section: RULIOLOGY — borrowed vocabulary, and what it corrected here
capacity.definition: how much a program can express. Wolfram measured it: 2-state machines top out at 0.151 against each other, 3-state machines reach 0.593 against 2-state ones, and a 10-state machine wins against **every** 2-state machine by holding a specialised sub-machine for each. **Measured here, and it did NOT transfer cleanly** — see the two entries below.

capacity is not monotone under sampling.term: capacity is not monotone under sampling
capacity is not monotone under sampling.section: RULIOLOGY — borrowed vocabulary, and what it corrected here
capacity is not monotone under sampling.definition: Wolfram got monotone gains by *exhaustively enumerating*; we sample. Adding dimensions to a sampled space dilutes it faster than it opens it. Measured on `arrangement`: lowering one gene's floor raised reachable clustering **4.736 → 6.588**, but adding two more capacity dimensions *lowered* it to 4.780 and 5.312. **Consequence for method:** a reachability probe by random sampling measures the PRIOR, not the reachable. The honest test of a capacity increase is to **train inside it**.

a pinned gene is not a binding constrain.term: a pinned gene is not a binding constraint
a pinned gene is not a binding constrain.section: RULIOLOGY — borrowed vocabulary, and what it corrected here
a pinned gene is not a binding constrain.definition: recorded because this studio asserted the opposite and was wrong. `cluster_tight` sat exactly on its 0.02 floor, which was read as "the vocabulary runs out". Widening the floor to 0.005 and retraining moved the score from **0.8238 to 0.8240** — nothing. The gene drifted off the floor to 0.0313 and clustering turned out to have the *largest* margin of any fact (0.722). The real limiter was `verticality` (margin 0.196, band width 0.176) and `alignment` (0.204, width 0.061) — narrow because they came from 5 regions of ONE scan. **The lever was more scans, not more capacity.** `pinned()` reports where a winner rests, which is not the same as where it is held back. ---

the column rule.section: THE HUMAN TERMINAL — and the -ologies that staff it
the column rule.definition: does the fact hold with **nobody there**? Gravity does → PHYSICS. A just-noticeable-difference does not, and neither does a group's preference → THE HUMAN, **even though both are rigorously measured**. Without this rule, "we measured it" launders every human fact into the physics column and the terminal stays empty while looking full.

taste.section: THE HUMAN TERMINAL — and the -ologies that staff it
taste.definition: no measurement can settle whether a thing is worth **wanting**. You can measure what something is and what it does; whether it should exist bottoms out in a person, and there is nowhere further to go. → `core/taste.py` (human-writable only)

the physics measure vector.section: THE HUMAN TERMINAL — and the -ologies that staff it
the physics measure vector.definition: the ~6 honest physical axes taste is learned *over* (`skill_gap`, `punishes_naive`, `learnability`, `headroom`, …). **This one terminates at PHYSICS, correctly:** the axes are physics; only the *weights* on them are taste. A reward model over raw artifacts needs thousands of labels; six interpretable axes need a dozen comparisons. → `core/preference.py`

the preference loop.section: THE HUMAN TERMINAL — and the -ologies that staff it
the preference loop.definition: taste elicited as **comparisons**, never declared as numbers, because a person can reliably say which of two things they prefer and cannot reliably say what weight they put on an axis. → `core/preference_elicit.py`

fun.section: THE HUMAN TERMINAL — and the -ologies that staff it
fun.definition: subjective for one person and **structured across a group**, so it is measurable as a *distribution* even though it is not measurable as a *value* — the same reason a material is stored as a range and not an average. This is what makes the human terminal reachable at all.

cultural heritability.section: THE HUMAN TERMINAL — and the -ologies that staff it
cultural heritability.definition: the heritability formula with **cultures in place of specimens**: `V_between / (V_between + V_within)` says which parts of fun are **regional** (predictable from where a person is) and which are **personal** (varying as much inside a country as between countries, so no amount of sociology will predict them — you must ask the individual). Most arguments about "what players want" are that distinction, unmade.

psychophysics.section: THE HUMAN TERMINAL — and the -ologies that staff it
psychophysics.definition: the science of the **span** between a physical stimulus and a human sensation (just-noticeable-difference, Weber's law, measured since the 1860s). It answers "how precise does this have to be" with *whatever a person can actually tell apart at that distance*, instead of with an opinion.

the span.section: THE HUMAN TERMINAL — and the -ologies that staff it
the span.definition: emotion is neither terminal but the **distance between them**: a real law reaching a real person. Physics alone is a **cutscene** (lawful, nothing felt); the human alone is **asserted** (no physics under it — the taste of a bad game). Only a chain spanning both was actually felt. → `core/spine.py :: span()`

the player is the second terminal.term: the player is the second terminal
the player is the second terminal.section: THE HUMAN TERMINAL — and the -ologies that staff it
the player is the second terminal.definition: in development THE HUMAN is the operator's taste; in the shipped game it is the player. **The same slot, not an analogy** — which is why the rule that keeps the engineering honest (nothing may be its own reason) is the rule that makes a story feel real.

a choice that costs something.section: THE HUMAN TERMINAL — and the -ologies that staff it
a choice that costs something.definition: a choice with no cost is a **menu**. The cost is what makes the player the *cause* of what follows rather than the witness of it, and only a cause can be a terminal. ---

timeline.section: TIMELINES — the mega membrane, and there is more than one
timeline.definition: anything with a beginning and an end is a boundary, so a timeline is a membrane like any other. **There is no single clock** — only nested ones, containing each other exactly as `universe ⊃ planet ⊃ section ⊃ cell` does: ``` cultural → development → story → session → beat ``` Each **gates** the one inside it: a condition measured on the outer timeline is what releases the inner one's dial. → `core/spine.py :: TIMELINES, gates()`

cultural time.section: TIMELINES — the mega membrane, and there is more than one
cultural time.definition: a demographic is a **trajectory, not a snapshot**. What is fun in a place in 2026 is not what was fun there in 2016. Treating an audience as fixed is the same mistake as storing a material as an average instead of a range.

development time.section: TIMELINES — the mega membrane, and there is more than one
development time.definition: this project's own history is a boundary with an inside and an outside, which is why `THE_WORKFLOW.md` could only be written by reading the git chronology **in order**. The sequence is the structure, not a presentation choice.

story time.section: TIMELINES — the mega membrane, and there is more than one
story time.definition: the player's journey is the dial between two states of the world, so the story is the outermost dial the player can actually reach, with **gates** along it.

a release is a gate.section: TIMELINES — the mega membrane, and there is more than one
a release is a gate.definition: a gate is a dial held until a *measured* condition holds, and a release condition is measured on the **cultural** timeline. So "when do we ship" stops being a calendar guess and becomes a reading of whether the audience's trajectory has crossed the bar.

the human stands at the boundary.term: the human stands at the boundary
the human stands at the boundary.section: TIMELINES — the mega membrane, and there is more than one
the human stands at the boundary.definition: cultural time and development time are two membranes, and a person is the only thing that can look across the seam and decide what to build. **Not a management role — a port**: the one place those two membranes touch. Every science this project recruits, what **number** it supplies, and whether it has actually been used. Machine-readable: `core/spine.py :: OLOGIES`, `staffing()`. **Read the gap, not the list.** One full column and two nearly empty ones is precisely why this vocabulary scored CUTSCENE against its own span test. An -ology is not decoration — it is where a terminal's numbers come from, and a terminal with no science behind it stays empty however much is built on the other side. ---
